papers.title: Suppression of corticospinal excitability by sleep spindles without increase in GABAergic inhibition
papers.summary: Using real-time EEG-triggered TMS during NREM sleep, this study found that corticospinal excitability is reduced during sleep spindles compared to spindle-free sleep, but no significant modulation of GABA-A-mediated SICI was observed. The findings suggest spindle-related excitability suppression is not due to increased GABAergic inhibition, while slow oscillations may have distinct effects.

papers.title: Specification dependence of EEG theta/alpha ratio associations with cognitive impairment: a multiverse analysis
papers.summary: This study applied multiverse analysis to assess the robustness of EEG theta/alpha ratio associations with cognitive impairment across 1,280 pipelines, varying preprocessing, spectral, spatial, and statistical decisions. Results were specification-dependent, with significant associations in most universes only when using specific combinations (e.g., ICA with FFT/Welch power), but higher theta/alpha ratios consistently correlated with greater cognitive impairment.

papers.title: A Dual Soft Attention Network for Automatic Sleep Staging via Single-Lead Electrocardiogram Signals.
papers.summary: The paper proposes SleepECGNet, a dual-attention deep learning method for automatic sleep staging using single-lead ECG signals, which extracts multi-scale features and uses SE and Luong attention to focus on relevant segments. Experiments on HMC, MGH, and SHHS1 datasets demonstrated improved classification performance, and transfer learning was applied to sleep apnea recognition.

papers.title: Cortical layer 6b mediates state-dependent changes in brain activity and effects of orexin on waking and sleep.
papers.summary: The study silenced cortical layer 6b (L6b) neurons in mice and recorded EEG, finding slowed theta frequency during wake and REM sleep and reduced total EEG power, especially in NREM sleep. L6b silencing also altered the response to orexin infusion, indicating a role in state-dependent brain oscillations.

papers.title: Tracking propagating cortical activity in MEG/EEG with a bilinear state-space model
papers.summary: This paper presents a bilinear state-space model that jointly tracks the oscillatory time course and migrating spatial topography of propagating cortical activity from MEG/EEG, evaluated on simulated and empirical occipital alpha data. The model outperformed traditional inverse solutions in recovering traveling waves and did not fabricate propagation for stationary sources.

papers.title: An Evidence-Aware Framework for EEG Microstate Analysis: Improved Sensitivity to Alzheimer's Disease and Ageing
papers.summary: This paper introduces an evidence-aware framework for EEG microstate analysis that retains template evidence at each GFP peak, deriving new descriptors (high-evidence episode duration/rate, null-state LZC). Across four datasets and multiple models, trajectory-derived features showed increased sensitivity to Alzheimer's disease and ageing compared to conventional hard-label methods.

papers.title: SingLEM: Single-Channel Large EEG Model.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: This paper introduces SingLEM, a self-supervised EEG foundation model that maps each channel independently, trained on 71 public datasets, and shows that concatenated channel representations plus an SVM outperform other methods across motor imagery and cognitive tasks under leave-one-subject-out evaluation. The model supports montage-flexible feature extraction and electrode-level spatial analysis.

papers.title: Sleep timing regulates mood: A multilevel-EEG study of daily life.
papers.summary: This observational study of 258 adults used Dreem2 EEG headbands to examine bidirectional daily associations between sleep and mood, finding a negative feedback loop where higher evening positive affect predicts later sleep onset and later onset predicts lower next-day positive affect, independent of sleep quality. Personality traits like extraversion amplified this effect, while neuroticism and alexithymia attenuated it.

papers.title: FoME: A foundation model for EEG using adaptive temporal-lateral attention scaling.
papers.journal: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
papers.summary: The paper presents FoME, a foundation model for EEG that uses adaptive temporal-lateral attention scaling and time-frequency fusion embedding, pre-trained on 1.7TB of EEG data. FoME achieves state-of-the-art performance across four downstream tasks including classification and forecasting, demonstrating its potential for brain-computer interfaces and clinical diagnostics.

papers.title: An Intraoperative EEG Biomarker for Postoperative Delirium Predicting Based on Interpretable Deep Learning Framework.
papers.summary: Using interpretable deep learning on intraoperative EEG from 71 older patients, the study identified a frontal EEG biomarker (2-12 Hz oscillations) that predicted postoperative delirium with high accuracy (AUC 0.911). External validation confirmed generalizability, supporting objective intraoperative risk stratification.

papers.title: Disrupted Sensorimotor Integration, Rather Than Regional Cortical Activation, Is Associated with Force Sense Deficits in Chronic Ankle Instability: A Partial Directed Coherence Analysis.
papers.summary: This study investigated sensorimotor network connectivity in chronic ankle instability (CAI) during ankle force-matching tasks using EEG and EMG with partial directed coherence analysis. Findings indicate that force sense deficits in CAI are associated with disrupted cortico-cortical and cortico-muscular connectivity, rather than altered regional cortical activity, highlighting the importance of network-level integration for rehabilitation.

papers.title: Frequency-aware transformer networks for robust and generalizable EEG-based seizure detection.
papers.summary: The paper introduces BrainXNet, a multi-scale spectro-temporal attention framework for EEG seizure detection. It achieves state-of-the-art accuracies of 99.1% on CHB-MIT and 98.4% on TUH, with strong cross-dataset generalization and robustness to noise, suggesting its potential for real-time clinical use.

papers.title: Reduced EEG Complexity and Its Association with Social Communication in Adults with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Multiscale Entropy Study
papers.summary: In adults with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), EEG multiscale entropy (MSE) at longer scales was reduced compared to controls across rest and movie conditions, and this reduction was associated with higher ADOS-2 Social Affect scores. Event-related MSE changes also showed attenuated differentiation between social and non-social windows in ASD.

papers.title: Heterogeneity of Brain Dynamics in Genetic and Psychiatric Conditions
papers.summary: This preprint analyzes resting-state EEG from 4,812 individuals across psychiatric conditions and genetic variants, establishing normative developmental trajectories. It finds psychiatric conditions show small transdiagnostic deviations, while rare genetic variants have larger distinct signatures, and provides an open resource for benchmarking.

papers.title: Noninvasive and objective near-real-time detection of pain changes during tonic fluctuating noxious heat stimulation.
papers.summary: This study trained deep learning models on physiological signals (EEG, electrodermal activity, heart rate, pupil diameter, facial expressions) to detect pain decreases during tonic fluctuating noxious heat in 42 healthy participants. Combining electrodermal activity, heart rate, and pupil diameter achieved optimal classification (AUC=0.854, accuracy=76.8%), with electrodermal activity being the most informative signal, enabling near-real-time detection of spontaneous pain changes.

papers.title: Prognostic assessment of comatose patients after cardiac arrest: construction of a simplified monitoring EEG risk score across different time windows.
papers.summary: This article constructs a Simplified EEG Risk Score (SERS) for poor neurological outcome prediction in comatose patients after cardiac arrest. SERS achieved high AUCs (0.912, 0.893, 0.881) across time windows, outperforming individual EEG features and clinical predictors, offering reliable risk stratification.

papers.title: Non-unitary reproducibility of an EEG-DMN-like sensor-level proxy: metric-family, task-window and paradigm effects across internally oriented tasks.
papers.summary: This study evaluates the reproducibility of an EEG-based default-mode network (DMN) proxy across internally oriented tasks, testing spectral and connectivity measures. Results show that spectral markers (posterior alpha suppression, frontal theta enhancement) are directionally consistent across cohorts, but connectivity measures are estimator- and task-dependent, indicating that the proxy is not a unitary biomarker.

papers.title: Perspectives in Conducting Task-Based Research in Pediatric Surgical Epilepsy Patients.
papers.summary: This paper retrospectively analyzed participation patterns in task-based stereo-electroencephalography (sEEG) research in 66 pediatric epilepsy patients, finding 89% consented and most with comorbidities participated in at least one task, though global developmental delay was associated with reduced time on tasks. The authors propose strategies to accommodate pediatric patients in such research.

papers.title: Neurophysiological subtyping of schizophrenia reveals a reproducible phenotype with temporoparietal circuit disruptions.
papers.summary: Using source-localized resting-state EEG functional connectivity, the authors identified two reproducible schizophrenia subtypes via sparse k-means clustering in discovery and replication cohorts; one subtype showed temporoparietal disconnection while the other had preserved connectivity, and connectivity predicted symptom severity only in the disconnected subtype.

papers.title: Mapping and modulating brain dynamics in aging and neurodegeneration with electroencephalography and integrated neurotechnologies in primates.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes EEG methodologies in non-human primates (NHPs) for studying aging and neurodegeneration, highlighting EEG signatures, multimodal integration with fMRI/MEG/NIRS, and neuromodulation techniques such as TMS and tDCS. It emphasizes translational relevance for human neuroscience, including examples in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease models.

papers.title: Advanced imaging-integrated rTMS therapy for frontal network recovery after traumatic brain injury.
papers.summary: In a retrospective multicenter cohort study of 48 adults with traumatic brain injury, documented exposure to high-frequency left-DLPFC rTMS was associated with greater improvement in executive function scores (FAB and MoCA) and enhanced frontal-network biomarkers (N100/P200, fNIRS HbO, fMRI connectivity) compared to standard rehabilitation alone.

papers.title: Towards adaptive flight support: EEG-based cognitive workload monitoring in aviation scenarios.
papers.summary: In a simulated Cessna 172 flight, EEG recordings revealed phase-dependent desynchronization of alpha and beta rhythms in frontal regions during take-off, turning, and landing, and increased global efficiency and transitivity in brain networks, along with enhanced PLV and PDC connectivity, indicating higher cognitive load during demanding flight phases.

papers.title: Electroencephalographic Signatures of Methylphenidate in ADHD: A Systematic Review and 10 Recommendations for Future Research.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 44 studies examined EEG effects of methylphenidate in ADHD. The most consistent finding was increased P3 amplitude, but EEG did not meet criteria as a treatment-response biomarker.

papers.title: Eccentricity confound in EEG-based visual attention decoding from gaze-fixated neural tracking of motion in natural videos.
papers.summary: The study investigates how visual eccentricity confounds EEG-based decoding of visual attention during natural video viewing under gaze fixation. Results show neural tracking is modulated by attention but poorer at larger eccentricities, revealing a significant confound for current decoding approaches.

papers.title: EEG Reactivity and Etiology as Prognostic Modifiers in Alpha and Theta Coma: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of alpha/theta coma found that overall 83.7% of patients had severe disability or death, but EEG reactivity was a significant prognostic modifier: nonreactive EEG had higher odds of mortality (OR 5.67) while reactive EEG increased odds of favorable outcome (OR 8.68). Etiology also influenced outcomes.

papers.title: Adult primary whole-brain cultures from Thy1-aSyn mice (Line 61) retain Parkinson's disease-relevant phenotypes.
papers.summary: This study established adult primary whole-brain cultures from Thy1-aSyn (Line 61) mice overexpressing human alpha-synuclein, maintaining key Parkinson's disease phenotypes including reduced neuronal viability, altered firing, and microgliosis. These cultures offer a novel in vitro model for studying aSyn-associated neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Multimodal EEG-HRV assessment of individual regulatory patterns: a perturbation-based approach toward precision psychiatry.
papers.summary: This pilot study used a perturbation-based EEG-HRV paradigm to assess cortico-autonomic regulation in 10 healthy participants. Findings showed high inter-individual variability, with coordinated changes in a subset, supporting feasibility for precision psychiatry.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Atrial Electrophysiology Across Animal Species and Humans: Enhancing Translation in Atrial Arrhythmia Research.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
papers.summary: This study systematically compared atrial electrophysiology across mice, rats, pigs, horses, and humans using uniform protocols. Porcine cardiomyocytes closely matched human depolarization, while early repolarization was uniquely pronounced in humans, linked to IKur expression; late repolarization scaled with cell size, and sex differences in humans were mimicked by pigs.

papers.title: A Hybrid Signal Processing and Deep Learning Framework for Parkinson's Disease Classification and Determination of ON and OFF Medication Condition.
papers.summary: The paper presents a hybrid framework combining Variational Mode Decomposition and Wavelet Coherence with a 2D-CNN to classify Parkinson's disease and ON/OFF medication states from EEG signals. The model achieved high accuracy (99.80%) in classifying PD versus healthy controls, outperforming existing methods.

papers.title: Subregion-specific input organization of prefrontal-projecting basal forebrain cholinergic neurons and weakened striatal-NBM inhibitory transmission in 5xFAD mice.
papers.summary: Using monosynaptic tracing, the study reveals distinct input patterns to prefrontal-projecting cholinergic neurons in the NBM and HDB, with NBM neurons receiving prominent striatal input. Optogenetic experiments confirmed monosynaptic GABAergic inhibition from striatal dMSNs weakened in 5xFAD mice, an Alzheimer's disease model.

papers.title: Time-Frequency Analysis of Muscle Activation Patterns during the Instep Kick in Elite and Amateur Soccer Players.
papers.summary: This study compared time-frequency muscle activation patterns during the instep kick between elite and amateur soccer players using surface electromyography and Morlet wavelet analysis. Elites showed a more temporally focused pre-contact activation centered on mid-frequency components of the biceps femoris, while amateurs relied more on higher-frequency medial gastrocnemius activity during follow-through, indicating phase-specific redistributions in muscle and frequency-band activity.

papers.title: Valproate-induced hyperammonemic encephalopathy versus asymptomatic hyperammonemia in adults with epilepsy: a cross-sectional study
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study compared adults with epilepsy on valproate who developed hyperammonemic encephalopathy (VHE) versus asymptomatic hyperammonemia. VHE patients had higher ammonia levels and shorter valproate duration, but no differences in valproate trough or liver enzymes; diffuse EEG slowing and prior cerebral infarction were more common in VHE, and all recovered after valproate withdrawal.

papers.title: Role Framing and Trust in Medical AI: Evidence from a Scenario Experiment and EEG.
papers.summary: This study examined how role framing (expert vs. companion) of medical AI influences trust using a scenario experiment and EEG. Expert framing increased perceived professionalism, while companion framing increased social presence, with both linked to trust, but EEG frontal-midline theta differences were exploratory and showed no behavioral trust differences, suggesting nuanced effects.

papers.title: Optical control of the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus kisspeptin neuronal network with a photoswitchable peptide that drives luteinizing hormone release in female mice.
papers.summary: This study developed a photoswitchable TacR3 agonist (azo-senktide) to optically control arcuate kisspeptin neurons in female mice. Light-activated azo-senktide depolarized Kiss1ARH neurons in slices and elicited a time-locked LH pulse in vivo at an intermediate dose, demonstrating that neurokinin B signaling dynamics regulate pulsatile LH release.

papers.title: EEG Artifacts During Pediatric Cardiopulmonary Bypass: Three Illustrative Cases.
papers.summary: This paper reports three illustrative cases of EEG artifacts during pediatric cardiopulmonary bypass, highlighting their occurrence and potential sources. The cases likely demonstrate characteristic artifact patterns to aid in recognition and interpretation.

papers.title: [A case of bilateral open-lip schizencephaly with West syndrome due to variant of PAFAH1B1 gene and literature review].
papers.journal: Zhonghua yi xue yi chuan xue za zhi = Zhonghua yixue yichuanxue zazhi = Chinese journal of medical genetics
papers.summary: This case report and literature review describes a 4-month-old boy with bilateral open-lip schizencephaly and West syndrome due to a de novo frameshift variant in PAFAH1B1. The variant was classified as pathogenic, and analysis of 36 cases showed consistent phenotypes including infantile spasms, developmental delay, and cortical malformations, highlighting the importance of early genetic testing.

papers.title: Correction: EEG-guided sevoflurane anesthesia vs. standard care in pediatric emergence delirium: a grade-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis.
papers.summary: This is a correction notice for a previously published systematic review and meta-analysis on EEG-guided sevoflurane anesthesia and pediatric emergence delirium.

papers.title: Correction: Machine learning-based lateralization and localization of seizure onset in focal cortical dysplasia patients using ictal scalp EEG.
papers.summary: This document is a published erratum correcting an earlier article on machine learning-based lateralization and localization of seizure onset in focal cortical dysplasia patients using ictal scalp EEG. It does not report new findings but serves to rectify the original publication.

papers.title: Using the OPTIMAL Theory to Optimize Aerodynamics in Respiratory Training for Healthy Adults and Individuals With Parkinson's Disease.
papers.journal: International journal of language & communication disorders
papers.summary: This randomized controlled trial investigated whether applying OPTIMAL theory strategies during respiratory muscle strength training improves immediate respiratory motor performance in healthy adults and individuals with Parkinson's disease. Results showed significant improvements in peak expiratory flow in both OPTIMAL groups compared to controls, but no changes in cough strength.

papers.title: Longitudinal Evidence on Natural History, Nonoperative Management, and Multimodal Surveillance in Mild to Moderate Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This scoping review maps longitudinal evidence on natural history, nonoperative management, and multimodal surveillance in mild to moderate degenerative cervical myelopathy. Findings suggest that mild to moderate disease is not uniformly stable, and multimodal follow-up appears more informative than single-scale monitoring.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
